what: Brown & Brown is an insurance broker. It arranges property, casualty and employee benefits insurance for businesses and individuals, earning commissions from insurers rather than fees from clients in most cases.
customers: Small and mid-sized businesses, public entities, professional firms and individuals across the United States and internationally.
money: commercial and personal insurance placed for clients
specialty programmes underwritten for niche industries
excess and surplus lines placed through other brokers
moat: Hundreds of local offices run with unusual autonomy, which keeps client relationships personal, combined with specialty programmes where it controls the whole product.
risks: Commercial insurance rate softening reduces commission income
Debt of about $8 billion from continuous acquisitions
Acquisition multiples for brokers have risen, making deals less attractive
Analyst targets imply the shares are already fully valued
opportunities: Revenue grew about 23% last year and about 18% a year over three years
Brokerage requires almost no capital, so cash flow converts well
A long record of buying small brokers and raising their margins
watch: Organic revenue growth and the adjusted operating margin.
